Cucumber, as sold from Moldova Noua (mining area M) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 370 µg/kg, against 160 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the cucumber came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cucumber" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cucumber-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of cucumber, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for cucumber, as sold on this basis in the completed cucumber ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach cucumber

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach cucumber comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Cucumber, as sold from Location A1 (industrial-affected area) had total mercury higher at 38.5 µg/kg, against 0.87 µg/kg for Control (grocery store >55 km from any power plant) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, cucumber, as sold from Ruschita (mining area R) (mining-affected area) had Mn higher at 6,730 µg/kg, against 450 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that cucumber, as sold from private garden (industrial-affected area) had lead higher at 82.3 µg/kg, against 20.5 µg/kg for private garden in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ristevska2026-north-macedonia-vegetables-lead|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Temelkovska Ristevska K, Pavlovska G, Petrović SM, Savić S, Blazhevska T, Trajkovska Petkoska A · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ristevska2026-north-macedonia-vegetables-lead">Dietary Lead Intake from Vegetables Grown near Industrial Pollution Sources and Associated Public Health Risks: Case Studies from North Macedonia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pollutants 2026, 6, 58</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ristevska2026-north-macedonia-vegetables-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into cucumber?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, cucumber from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than cucumber from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cucumber, as sold from Moldova Noua (mining area M) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 370 µg/kg, against 160 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-cucumber-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-cucumber-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of cucumber have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of cucumber have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for cucumber, peeled or flesh (1.6 µg/kg) and highest for cucumber, as sold (102 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-cucumber" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-cucumber" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in cucumber?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in cucumber?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, cucumber, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (4 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (520 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (2 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (11 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-cucumber-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-cucumber-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in cucumber is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in cucumber is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 10 results from 5 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup
